en: Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4); Tikatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (5). 23.9. The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika);
The Triplet of That Which Leads to Accumulation (Ācayagāmittika).

Conditioned by a state that is neither wholesome nor leading to accumulation, a wholesome state leading to accumulation arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are six; ... [and so on] ... under non-disappearance condition there are six.

Conditioned by a state that is neither wholesome nor leading to disintegration, a wholesome state leading to disintegration arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are three; ... [and so on] ... under non-disappearance condition there are three.
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor leading to neither-accumulation-nor-disintegration, an indeterminate state leading to neither-accumulation-nor-disintegration [arises].
A state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. There are five [answers] for root; five for predominance …pe… five for non-disappearance.
